chapter: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
title: The Smith brothers Joe and Luke
summary: Joe Smith was a lyrical plunger-muted melody player and Luke a legitimate pit trumpeter in Blackbirds and shows.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Joe -- Now there was three brothers. There was Pop, Russell Smith, --
-- and there was Joe and there was Luke.
Yeah. Now Joe Smith did a lot of stuff for the Broadway shows that there was going at that time, for instance, --
Joe was more jazz orientated, wasn't he, or was he?
Not too much jazz as he was lyrical.

He was very lyrical. He was a very lyrical trumpet player. He played a lot of melody. He used to play with the 2 cocked plunger and he would get a sound playing melody with that cocked plunger with the most beautiful vibrato you ever heard, and even ladies used to listen to him. They used to go crazy over him playing like that. And he never really played jazz, no.
Now Luke was a legitimate trumpet player like Russell was, the other brother. Now, he played in Blackbirds and shows like that.

He was a pit trumpet player. He was that type of trumpet player. I never heard him play but everybody knew what a trumpet player he was. There was that whole three brothers, all three of them were great trumpet players.
